## Latent Briefing Overview

Latent Briefing is about efficient memory sharing for multi-agent systems via KV cache compaction. Instead of compressing text, it compresses the model's internal representations.

## How It Works

The worker maintains a persistent KV cache of the orchestrator's trajectory across calls. On each call, the orchestrator's updated trajectory is forward passed through the worker model with KV prefix caching, the trajectory's KV cache is compacted using task-specific queries as the relevance signal, and the worker agent is initialized with this compacted KV cache.

The method uses task-adaptive relevance where attention scores between the task prompt's query vectors and the trajectory's KV cache keys reveal which parts of the context are relevant, and constructs a compact KV cache using important keys, bias corrections for missing keys, and reconstructed values via ridge regression.

## Landscape Report: KV Cache Compaction for Agent / Multi-Turn LLM Inference (2025-2026)

The space is **extremely active**. There are multiple papers and products addressing KV cache management for agentic workloads, and several that come close to -- or partially overlap with -- the specific idea of "incremental attention-matching-style KV compaction between agent tool calls to bound memory growth." I will organize findings by relevance.

---

### HIGH RELEVANCE -- Papers that closely overlap with the target idea

#### 1. Latent Briefing (Ramp Labs, 2026)
- **Title:** "Latent Briefing: Efficient Memory Sharing for Multi-Agent Systems via KV Cache Compaction"
- **Authors/Org:** Ramp Labs
- **Venue:** Announced on X/Twitter; no confirmed arxiv link found
- **URL:** [Ramp Labs Twitter](https://x.com/RampLabs/status/2042660310851449223)
- **SIMILARITY: VERY HIGH.** This work uses attention-based relevance scoring (attention scores between task prompt queries and trajectory KV cache keys) to compact a worker agent's KV cache *between calls*. It uses ridge regression to reconstruct values and bias corrections for removed keys. Evaluated with Claude Sonnet 4 as orchestrator and Qwen-14B as worker on LongBench v2. Achieved 42-57% worker token reduction, 21-31% total token reduction, +3pp accuracy. **This is the closest match to "incremental attention-matching-style KV compaction between agent tool calls."** The key distinction is that it targets inter-agent memory sharing (orchestrator-to-worker) rather than intra-agent compaction within a single agent's tool-call loop.

#### 2. SideQuest (Kariyappa & Suh, Feb 2026)
- **Title:** "SideQuest: Model-Driven KV Cache Management for Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning"
- **Authors:** Sanjay Kariyappa, G. Edward Suh
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **URL:** [arXiv 2602.22603](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22603)
- **SIMILARITY: HIGH.** Directly addresses KV cache compression for multi-turn agentic reasoning with tool calls. Uses the LRM itself to reason about token usefulness in a shared-context parallel architecture. Identifies that agentic workloads make heuristic-based pruning insufficient because token importance changes across tool-call rounds. Focuses on evicting stale tool-call results. **The key difference from your idea:** it uses model-driven reasoning (the LLM itself decides what to evict) rather than an attention-matching algebraic approach.

#### 3. Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching (Zweiger et al., Feb 2026)
- **Title:** "Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching"
- **Authors:** Adam Zweiger, Xinghong Fu, Han Guo, Yoon Kim (MIT)
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (Feb 18, 2026); widely covered by VentureBeat, HackerNoon
- **URL:** [arXiv 2602.16284](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16284)
- **Code:** [github.com/adamzweiger/compaction](https://github.com/adamzweiger/compaction)
- **SIMILARITY: HIGH (method match, different application).** This is the core *method* -- attention matching to construct compact KV caches analytically (OLS/NNLS), achieving 50x compaction. However, the paper itself focuses on compaction as a general technique (long documents, prefill optimization), **not specifically on incremental application between agent tool calls**. Your idea would be applying this method in the agent-loop setting.

---

### MEDIUM-HIGH RELEVANCE -- Agent KV cache management, different mechanism

#### 4. Continuum / CacheTTL (Nov 2025, updated May 2026)
- **Title:** "Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live"
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **URL:** [arXiv 2511.02230](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02230)
- **What it does:** Introduces a time-to-live (TTL) mechanism for KV cache retention across agent tool calls. Addresses the problem that standard eviction policies discard KV cache during tool-call pauses, forcing expensive recomputation. Built on vLLM. **Focuses on retention/scheduling rather than compaction** -- it decides *how long to keep* cache entries, not how to compress them.

#### 5. SAGA (May 2026)
- **Title:** "SAGA: Workflow-Atomic Scheduling for AI Agent Inference on GPU Clusters"
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **URL:** [arXiv 2605.00528](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00528)
- **What it does:** Treats entire agent workflows as schedulable units, uses Agent Execution Graphs to predict KV cache reuse across tool-call boundaries. Measures show agents spend **38% of time regenerating discarded KV cache**. Achieves 1.64x task completion speedup on 64-GPU cluster. **Focuses on scheduling/retention, not compaction.** Complementary to compaction-between-turns.

#### 6. PBKV (May 2026)
- **Title:** "Efficient Serving for Dynamic Agent Workflows with Prediction-based KV-Cache Management"
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **URL:** [arXiv 2605.06472](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06472v1)
- **What it does:** Predicts future agent invocations and estimates reuse potential of cache entries to decide what to keep in GPU memory. Addresses dynamic multi-agent workflows. **Prediction-based retention, not compaction.**

#### 7. ACON (Kang et al., Oct 2025)
- **Title:** "ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents"
- **Authors:** Minki Kang et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint; also on OpenReview
- **URL:** [arXiv 2510.00615](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615)
- **What it does:** Text-level (not KV-level) context compression between agent turns. Uses natural-language compression guidelines optimized from paired trajectories. Reduces peak tokens by 26-54%. **Operates at the prompt/text level, not the KV cache level.** Gradient-free and works with closed-source models.

#### 8. Agent Memory Below the Prompt (Shkolnikov, Feb 2026)
- **Title:** "Agent Memory Below the Prompt: Persistent Q4 KV Cache for Multi-Agent LLM Inference on Edge Devices"
- **Authors:** Yakov Pyotr Shkolnikov
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint
- **URL:** [arXiv 2603.04428](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04428)
- **What it does:** Persists each agent's KV cache to disk in Q4 format between turns, reloads directly into attention layers. Achieves 136x TTFT improvement and 4x more agent contexts in memory. **Quantization + persistence, not compaction/compression of the cache content.**

---

### MEDIUM RELEVANCE -- Infrastructure and frameworks

#### 9. Segment-Level KV Cache Sharing (OpenReview, Oct 2025)
- **Title:** "Towards a Collaborative Memory for Agentic Workflow: Breaking the Prefix Barrier with Segment-Level KV Cache Sharing"
- **Venue:** OpenReview
- **URL:** [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=kgzBkyqg6Z)
- **What it does:** Decomposes KV cache into semantic segments for cross-agent reuse without prefix constraints. Built on vLLM/PageAttention. **Sharing mechanism, not compaction.**

#### 10. Microsoft Agent Framework -- Compaction (2026)
- **Title:** Compaction (part of Microsoft Agent Framework)
- **Venue:** Product documentation
- **URL:** [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/agents/conversations/compaction)
- **What it does:** Text-level compaction strategies (truncation, summarization, tool-result compaction) for agent conversation histories. Currently experimental. **Text-level, not KV-level.**

#### 11. FlashCompact / Morph (2026)
- **Title:** "FlashCompact: Every Context Compaction Method Compared"
- **Venue:** Morph blog / product
- **URL:** [morphllm.com/flashcompact](https://www.morphllm.com/flashcompact)
- **What it does:** Prevents context waste via WarpGrep (return only relevant code), Fast Apply (compact diffs), and verbatim deletion. Achieves 3-4x reduction in per-tool-call context consumption. **Text-level optimization for coding agents, not KV-level.**

---

### FOUNDATIONAL METHODS (general KV compression, not agent-specific)

#### 12. Baseten -- Neural KV Cache Compaction Survey (Apr 2026)
- **URL:** [baseten.co/research](https://www.baseten.co/research/towards-infinite-context-windows-neural-kv-cache-compaction/)
- Surveys STILL (perceiver bottleneck), Attention Matching, and Cartridges (gradient-based) approaches.

#### 13. KV Cache Transform Coding (ICLR 2026)
- **URL:** [arXiv 2511.01815](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01815) / [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/pdf/1cef9774f0f0cf7bb9e4b167882e3ad3ef8cde16.pdf)
- Published as conference paper at ICLR 2026. Lossy coding theory approach to KV compression.

#### 14. TurboQuant (Google, ICLR 2026)
- 3.5-bit KV cache quantization, 6x compression, near-zero accuracy loss.

#### 15. MemAgents Workshop (ICLR 2026)
- **URL:** [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=U51WxL382H)
- Workshop on memory for LLM-based agentic systems. Likely venue for related submissions.

---

### GAP ANALYSIS: Is anyone doing exactly "incremental attention-matching-style KV compaction between agent tool calls"?

**No single paper does exactly this.** The landscape breaks down as follows:

| Component | Who has it |
|---|---|
| Attention Matching for KV compaction | Zweiger et al. (2602.16284) -- the method |
| KV-level compaction applied to agent workloads | Latent Briefing (Ramp Labs) -- inter-agent, not intra-agent |
| Incremental compaction between tool calls | SideQuest (model-driven, not attention-matching) |
| KV cache retention/scheduling across tool calls | Continuum, SAGA, PBKV |
| Text-level agent context compression | ACON, Microsoft Agent Framework, FlashCompact |

**The closest threat is Latent Briefing (Ramp Labs)**, which applies attention-score-based KV compaction between agent calls, but it is designed for orchestrator-to-worker memory sharing in multi-agent systems, not for bounding a single agent's KV cache growth across its own tool-call loop.

**The specific combination of:**
1. Using Attention Matching (the algebraic OLS/NNLS method from Zweiger et al.)
2. Applied incrementally after each tool call
3. Within a single agent's inference loop
4. To bound memory growth as turns accumulate

...does not appear to be claimed by any existing paper. The pieces exist separately but have not been assembled in this specific configuration. However, Latent Briefing is close enough that you should read it carefully and position against it. SideQuest is also relevant as a contrasting approach (model-driven vs. algebraic).
